title: Bittensor Daily News: November 7, 2026

updates.headline: SN15 ORO publishes SMB Bench, testing delayed consequences across 90 simulated buying days
updates.summary: Announced November 6 at 22:18:53 UTC, SMB Bench v1.0 assigns models a produce wholesaler’s purchasing desk across 18 tasks: six synthetic businesses in normal, customer-response and supplier-disruption quarters. ORO publishes 485 scored runs from nine models, their tool traces and a reproducible summary script. Our independent arithmetic on its public scored rows matches the displayed mean simulated quarterly profit: GPT-6 Astra $7,749 versus the fixed buying rule’s $6,412; the other eight models finish below that rule on average. These are simulation scores, not earned business revenue. ORO’s earlier November 4 direction article described a forthcoming subnet workload; this benchmark release does not establish that mainnet replacement. Regrading requires access to a separately gated bundle, and the world generator is not released. No independent model run or regrading was performed.

updates.headline: SN17 separates Witness Pod runtime and adds render-cache safeguards
updates.summary: Announced or committed 2026-11-06 T 20:55:53 Z. PR83 merged at 20:55:53 UTC. The primary patch describes exact-request render caching, replay evidence separated from final results, and separate gateway/Pod packages. Frozen round inputs govern final saving while Finney membership stays in the gateway. The author reports extensive tests; those tests and a production rollout were not independently run. Fold this into the existing Witness tooling history rather than describe a new proven AI capability. November 7 follow-up commits reuse valid cached Pod access grants during polling and bound those validation reads by the request deadline. A 20:00:47 UTC commit separates admission POST limits from allocation/status GETs, including lease renewal, and adds bounded structured diagnostics. This addresses polling and admission contention in the implementation; live reliability was not tested.

updates.headline: SN71 Leadpoet improves Arena task publication, score retries and evidence matching
updates.summary: November 6–7 merges consolidate operator reliability work. Typed admission explanations avoid publishing raw provider prose; identity repair distinguishes missing evidence from transport failure. PR1105 makes daily task-bank publication atomic and requires old writers to be quiesced for migration. PR1106 binds score retries to output content and validates before immutable writes; PR1107 continues evidence matching past unrelated candidates. PR1103 adds bounded upload diagnostics. These are merged implementation changes, not proof of database migration, repaired production rounds, new customers or changed rewards. Earlier saved maintenance leads are folded into this entry. PR1110 merged November 7 at 20:19:01 UTC. It records Leadpoet operator authorization to use eligible Arena reasoning and execution trajectories for continued pretraining and supervised fine-tuning of its Sales LLM. The final scope explicitly leaves provider/source rights, miner consent and customer/privacy permissions separate. Dataset readiness remains false pending quality and rights checks; this is not evidence of a training run or a publicly released dataset.

updates.headline: SN127 Zils merges an opt-in adapter reward rule tied to paid API use
updates.summary: PR216 merged November 7 at 19:48:05 UTC. When enabled, the adapter track credits miners whose delivered customer adapters receive paid API use during the first 30 days after delivery. A configurable revenue cap limits the paid fraction of the adapter reward share using signed platform spend evidence and chain price inputs; unused share routes to the configured burn UID. Free, test-mode and operator use do not earn. The feature is off by default, and the signed ledger is a platform claim rather than independently audited revenue. PR215 also ranks graded job candidates by a smoothed delivery rate before their qualification quality band. These merges establish implementation changes, not mainnet activation, completed payouts, transaction burns or measured customer growth.
